t: Commemoratio  ad Laudes tantum: S. Martinæ Virginis et Martyris

b.e9291a97e2:
<r>℣.</r> Iube, domne, benedícere.
<r>Benedictio.</r> Oret voce pia pro nobis Virgo María.
<r>℟.</r> Amen.

<h>Lectio 1</h>
De libro Génesis
<r>Gen 4:13-16</r>
<n>13</n> Dixítque Cain ad Dóminum: Maior est iníquitas mea, quam ut véniam mérear.
<n>14</n> Ecce éicis me hódie a fácie terræ, et a fácie tua abscóndar, et ero vagus et prófugus in terra: omnis ígitur qui invénerit me, occídet me.
<n>15</n> Dixítque ei Dóminus: Nequáquam ita fiet: sed omnis qui occíderit Cain, séptuplum puniétur. Posuítque Dóminus Cain signum, ut non interfíceret eum omnis qui invenísset eum.
<r>℣.</r> Tu autem, Dómine, miserére nostri.
<r>℟.</r> Deo grátias.

<r>℟.</r> Immísit Dóminus sopórem in Adam, et tulit unam de costis eius: † Et ædificávit costam, quam túlerat Dóminus de Adam, in mulíerem, et addúxit eam ad Adam, ut vidéret quid vocáret eam:
* Et vocávit nomen eius Virágo, quia de viro sumpta est.
<r>℣.</r> Cumque obdormísset, tulit unam de costis eius, et replévit carnem pro ea.
<r>℟.</r> Et vocávit nomen eius Virágo, quia de viro sumpta est.
b.e6d411d0ec:
<r>℣.</r> Grant, Lord, a blessing.
<r>Benediction.</r> Oret voce pia pro nobis Virgo María.
<r>℟.</r> Amen.

<h>Reading 1</h>
Lesson from the book of Genesis
<r>Gen 4:13-16</r>
<n>13</n> And Cain said to the Lord: My iniquity is greater than that I may deserve pardon.
<n>14</n> Behold thou dost cast me out this day from the face of the earth, and I shall be hidden from thy face, and I shall be a vagabond and a fugitive on the earth: everyone, therefore, that findeth me, shall kill me.
<n>15</n> And the Lord said to him: No, it shall not be so: but whosoever shall kill Cain, shall be punished sevenfold. And the Lord set a mark upon Cain, that whosoever found him should not kill him.
<r>℣.</r> But thou, O Lord, have mercy upon us.
<r>℟.</r> Thanks be to God.

<r>℟.</r> The Lord caused a deep sleep to fall upon Adam, and He took one of his ribs. † And the rib which the Lord had taken from Adam made He a woman, and brought her unto Adam, to see what he would call her.
* And he called her name Woman, because she was taken out of Man.
<r>℣.</r> And while he slept He took one of his ribs, and closed up the flesh instead thereof.
<r>℟.</r> And he called her name Woman, because she was taken out of Man.
b.d458b3b6ca:
<r>℣.</r> Iube, domne, benedícere.
<r>Benedictio.</r> In omni tribulatióne et angústia subvéniat nobis pia Virgo Maria.
<r>℟.</r> Amen.

<h>Lectio 2</h>
<r>Gen 4:16-19</r>
<n>16</n> Egressúsque Cain a fácie Dómini, habitávit prófugus in terra ad orientálem plagam Eden.
<n>17</n> Cognóvit autem Cain uxórem suam, quæ concépit, et péperit Henoch: et ædificávit civitátem, vocavítque nomen eius ex nómine fílii sui, Henoch.
<n>18</n> Porro Henoch génuit Irad, et Irad génuit Mavíaël, et Mavíaël génuit Mathúsaël, et Mathúsaël génuit Lamech.
<n>19</n> Qui accépit duas uxóres.
<r>Gen 5:1-3</r>
<n>1</n> Hic est liber generatiónis Adam. In die qua creávit Deus hóminem, ad similitúdinem Dei fecit illum.
<n>2</n> Másculum et féminam creávit eos, et benedíxit illis: et vocávit nomen eórum Adam, in die quo creáti sunt.
<n>3</n> Vixit autem Adam centum trigínta annis: et génuit ad imáginem et similitúdinem suam, vocavítque nomen eius Seth.
<r>℣.</r> Tu autem, Dómine, miserére nostri.
<r>℟.</r> Deo grátias.

<r>℟.</r> Ubi est Abel frater tuus? dixit Dóminus ad Cain. Néscio, Dómine, numquid custos fratris mei sum ego? Et dixit ad eum: Quid fecísti?
* Ecce vox sánguinis fratris tui Abel clamat ad me de terra.
<r>℣.</r> Maledíctus eris super terram, quæ apéruit os suum, et suscépit sánguinem fratris tui de manu tua.
<r>℟.</r> Ecce vox sánguinis fratris tui Abel clamat ad me de terra.

<r>Benediction.</r> In omni tribulatióne et angústia subvéniat nobis pia Virgo Maria.

<h>Reading 2</h>
<r>Gen 4:16-19</r>
<n>16</n> And Cain went out from the face of the Lord, and dwelt as a fugitive on the earth, at the east side of Eden.
<n>17</n> And Cain knew his wife, and she conceived, and brought forth Henoch: and he built a city, and called the name thereof by the name of his son Henoch.
<n>18</n> And Henoch begot Irad, and Irad begot Maviael, and Maviael begot Mathusael, and Mathusael begot Lamech:
<n>19</n> Who took two wives.
<r>Gen 5:1-3</r>
<n>1</n> This is the book of the generation of Adam. In the day that God created man, he made him to the likeness of God.
<n>2</n> He created them male and female; and blessed them: and called their name Adam, in the day when they were created.
<n>3</n> And Adam lived a hundred and thirty years, and begot a son to his own image and likeness, and called his name Seth.
<r>℣.</r> But thou, O Lord, have mercy upon us.
<r>℟.</r> Thanks be to God.

<r>℟.</r> The Lord said unto Cain: Where is Abel thy brother? Lord, I know not am I my brother's keeper? And He said unto him What hast thou done?
* Behold, the voice of thy brother Abel's blood crieth unto Me from the ground.
<r>℣.</r> Cursed shalt thou be upon the earth, which hath opened her mouth to receive thy brother's blood from thy hand.
<r>℟.</r> Behold, the voice of thy brother Abel's blood crieth unto Me from the ground.
b.0340b4acea:
<r>℣.</r> Iube, domne, benedícere.
<r>Benedictio.</r> Ad societátem cívium supernórum perdúcat nos Regína Angelórum.
<r>℟.</r> Amen.

<h>Lectio 3</h>
Ex Epístola sancti Ambrósii Epíscopi ad Sirícium Papam
<r>Epist. 81, alias 7, post initium</r>
<c>D</c>e via perversitátis prodúntur dícere: Virgo concépit, sed non virgo generávit. Pótuit ergo virgo concípere, non pótuit virgo generáre, cum semper concéptus præcédat, partus sequátur? Sed, si doctrínis non créditur sacerdótum, credátur oráculis Christi; credátur mónitis Angelórum dicéntium: Quia non est impossíbile Deo omne verbum; credátur Sýmbolo Apostolórum, quod Ecclésia Romána intemerátum semper custódit et servat. Audívit María vocem Angeli, et, quæ ante díxerat: Quómodo fiet istud; non de fide generatiónis intérrogans, respóndit póstea: Ecce ancílla Dómini, contíngat mihi secúndum verbum tuum.
<r>℣.</r> Tu autem, Dómine, miserére nostri.
<r>℟.</r> Deo grátias.

<r>℟.</r> Virgo parens Christi, paritúra Deum genuísti: fúlgida stella maris, nos prótege, nos tueáris:
* Dum paris, et gaudes, Cantant cæli ágmina laudes.
<r>℣.</r> Intercéde pia pro nobis Virgo María.
<r>℟.</r> Dum paris, et gaudes, Cantant cæli ágmina laudes.
<r>℣.</r> Glória Patri, et Fílio, * et Spirítui Sancto.
<r>℟.</r> Cantant cæli ágmina laudes.

<r>Te Deum</r>
<c>T</c>e Deum laudámus: * te Dóminum confitémur.
Te ætérnum Patrem * omnis terra venerátur.
Tibi omnes Ángeli, * tibi Cæli, et univérsæ Potestátes:
Tibi Chérubim et Séraphim * incessábili voce proclámant:
<n>(Fit reverentia)</n> Sanctus, Sanctus, Sanctus * Dóminus Deus Sábaoth.
Pleni sunt cæli et terra * maiestátis glóriæ tuæ.
Te gloriósus * Apostolórum chorus,
Te Prophetárum * laudábilis númerus,
Te Mártyrum candidátus * laudat exércitus.
Te per orbem terrárum * sancta confitétur Ecclésia,
Patrem * imménsæ maiestátis;
Venerándum tuum verum * et únicum Fílium;
Sanctum quoque * Paráclitum Spíritum.
Tu Rex glóriæ, * Christe.
Tu Patris * sempitérnus es Fílius.
<n>(Fit reverentia)</n> Tu, ad liberándum susceptúrus hóminem: * non horruísti Vírginis úterum.
Tu, devícto mortis acúleo, * aperuísti credéntibus regna cælórum.
Tu ad déxteram Dei sedes, * in glória Patris.
Iudex créderis * esse ventúrus.
<n>(Sequens versus dicitur flexis genibus)</n> Te ergo quǽsumus, tuis fámulis súbveni, * quos pretióso sánguine redemísti.
Ætérna fac cum Sanctis tuis * in glória numerári.
Salvum fac pópulum tuum, Dómine, * et bénedic hereditáti tuæ.
Et rege eos, * et extólle illos usque in ætérnum.
Per síngulos dies * benedícimus te.
<n>(Fit reverentia, secundum consuetudinem)</n> Et laudámus nomen tuum in sǽculum, * et in sǽculum sǽculi.
Dignáre, Dómine, die isto * sine peccáto nos custodíre.
Miserére nostri, Dómine, * miserére nostri.
Fiat misericórdia tua, Dómine, super nos, * quemádmodum sperávimus in te.
In te, Dómine, sperávi: * non confúndar in ætérnum.

<h>Reading 3</h>
From the letter of Blessed Ambrose, bishop of Milan, to Pope Siricius
<r>Epist. 81, alias 7</r>
<c>H</c>ow great is the madness of their dismal barkings, that the same persons should say that Christ could not be born of a virgin, and yet assert that women, after having given birth to human pledges, remain virgins? But if they will not believe the doctrines of the Clergy, let them believe the oracles of Christ, let them believe the admonitions of Angels who say, For with God nothing shall be impossible. Let them give credit to the Creed of the Apostles, which the Roman Church has always kept and preserved undefiled. Mary heard the voice of the Angel, and she who before had said “How shall this be?”, not asking from want of faith in the mode of generation, afterwards replied: “Behold the handmaid of the Lord, be it unto me according to thy word.”
<r>℣.</r> But thou, O Lord, have mercy upon us.
<r>℟.</r> Thanks be to God.

<r>℟.</r> Virgo parens Christi, paritúra Deum genuísti: fúlgida stella maris, nos prótege, nos tueáris:
* Dum paris, et gaudes, Cantant cæli ágmina laudes.
<r>℣.</r> Intercéde pia pro nobis Virgo María.
<r>℟.</r> Dum paris, et gaudes, Cantant cæli ágmina laudes.
<r>℣.</r> Glory be to the Father, and to the Son, * and to the Holy Ghost.
<r>℟.</r> Cantant cæli ágmina laudes.

<r>Te Deum</r>
<c>W</c>e praise thee, O God, * we acknowledge thee to be the Lord.
All the earth doth worship thee, * the Father everlasting.
To thee all Angels cry aloud, * the Heavens, and all the Powers therein.
To thee Cherubim and Seraphim * continually do cry.
<n>bow head</n> Holy, Holy, Holy * Lord God of Sabaoth;
Heaven and earth are full * of the Majesty of thy glory.
The glorious company of the Apostles * praise thee.
The goodly fellowship of the Prophets * praise thee.
The noble army of Martyrs * praise thee.
The holy Church throughout all the world * doth acknowledge thee;
The Father, * of an infinite Majesty.
Thine honourable, true, * and only Son;
Also the Holy Ghost, * the Comforter.
Thou art the King of Glory, * O Christ.
Thou art the everlasting * Son of the Father.
<n>During the following verse all make a profound bow:</n> When thou tookest upon thee to deliver man, * thou didst not abhor the Virgin's womb.
When thou hadst overcome the sharpness of death, * thou didst open the Kingdom of Heaven to all believers.
Thou sittest at the right hand of God, * in the glory of the Father.
We believe that thou shalt come * to be our Judge.
<n>Kneel for the following verse</n> We therefore pray thee, help thy servants, * whom thou hast redeemed with thy precious Blood.
Make them to be numbered with thy Saints, * in glory everlasting.
O Lord, save thy people, * and bless thine heritage.
Govern them, * and lift them up for ever.
Day by day * we magnify thee;
<n>During the following verse, by local custom, all make a profound bow.</n> And we worship thy Name * ever, world without end.
Vouchsafe, O Lord, to keep us * this day without sin.
O Lord, have mercy upon us, * have mercy upon us.
O Lord, let thy mercy lighten upon us, * as our trust is in thee.
O Lord, in thee have I trusted, * let me never be confounded.

b.84e5b06554:
<h>Oratio</h>
<c>K</c>ýrie, eléison. Christe, eléison. Kýrie, eléison.
<n><k>Pater Noster</k> dicitur secreto usque ad <k>Et ne nos indúcas in tentatiónem:</k></n>
<c>P</c>ater noster, qui es in cælis, sanctificétur nomen tuum: advéniat regnum tuum: fiat volúntas tua, sicut in cælo et in terra. Panem nostrum cotidiánum da nobis hódie: et dimítte nobis débita nostra, sicut et nos dimíttimus debitóribus nostris:
<r>℣.</r> Et ne nos indúcas in tentatiónem:
<r>℟.</r> Sed líbera nos a malo.

<r>℣.</r> Dómine, exáudi oratiónem meam.
<r>℟.</r> Et clamor meus ad te véniat.
<c>O</c>rémus.
<c>D</c>eus, qui salútis ætérnæ, beátæ Maríæ virginitáte fecúnda, humáno géneri prǽmia præstitísti: tríbue, quǽsumus; ut ipsam pro nobis intercédere sentiámus, per quam merúimus auctórem vitæ suscípere, Dóminum nostrum Iesum Christum Fílium tuum:
<h>Q</h>ui tecum vivit et regnat in unitáte Spíritus Sancti, Deus, per ómnia sǽcula sæculórum.
<r>℟.</r> Amen.

<r>Commemoratio S. Martinæ Virginis et Martyris</r>
<r>Ant.</r> Veni, elécta mea, et ponam in te thronum meum; quia concupívit Rex spéciem tuam.

<r>℣.</r> Adducéntur Regi Vírgines post eam.
<r>℟.</r> Próximæ eius afferéntur tibi.

<c>O</c>rémus.
<c>I</c>ndulgéntiam nobis, quǽsumus, Dómine, beáta Martínæ Virgo et Martyr implóret: quæ tibi grata semper éxstitit, et mérito castitátis, et tuæ professióne virtútis.
<h>P</h>er Dóminum nostrum Iesum Christum, Fílium tuum: qui tecum vivit et regnat in unitáte Spíritus Sancti, Deus, per ómnia sǽcula sæculórum.
<r>℟.</r> Amen.
b.a06d5bfb69:
<h>Prayer</h>
<c>L</c>ord have mercy upon us, Christ have mercy upon us, Lord have mercy upon us.
<n><k>Our Father</k> is said silently until <k>And lead us not into temptation:</k>.</n>
<c>O</c>ur Father, who art in heaven, Hallowed be thy name. Thy kingdom come. Thy will be done on earth as it is in heaven. Give us this day our daily bread. And forgive us our trespasses, as we forgive those who trespass against us.
<r>℣.</r> And lead us not into temptation:
<r>℟.</r> But deliver us from evil.

<r>℣.</r> O Lord, hear my prayer.
<r>℟.</r> And let my cry come unto thee.
<c>L</c>et us pray.
<c>O</c> God, Who, by the fruitful virginity of the Blessed Mary, hast given unto mankind the rewards of everlasting life; grant, we beseech thee, that we may continually feel the might of her intercession, through whom we have worthily received the Author of our life, our Lord Jesus Christ, thy Son:
<h>W</h>ho with thee liveth and reigneth, in the unity of the Holy Spirit, God, world without end.
<r>℟.</r> Amen.

<r>Commemoration of St. Martina, Virgin and Martyr</r>
<r>Ant.</r> Come, O My chosen one, and I will establish My throne in thee, for the King hath greatly desired thy beauty.

<r>℣.</r> After her shall virgins be brought unto the King.
<r>℟.</r> Her fellows shall be brought unto thee.

<c>L</c>et us pray.
<c>O</c> Lord, we pray thee, that thy blessed handmaiden and witness Martina in whom Thou hast ever been well pleased, because of her worthy maidenhood and her mighty showing-forth of thy power, may entreat thy pardon on our behalf.
<h>T</h>hrough Jesus Christ, thy Son our Lord, Who liveth and reigneth with thee, in the unity of the Holy Ghost, God, world without end.
<r>℟.</r> Amen.
b.645c94462e:
<h>Martyrologium</h>
<c>P</c>rídie Kaléndas Februárii Luna vicésima tértia. Anno Dómini 2027
<h>A</h>ugústæ Taurinórum sancti Ioánnis Bosco, Confessóris, Societátis Salesiánæ ac Institúti Filiárum Maríæ Auxiliatrícis Fundatóris, animárum zelo et fídei propagándæ conspícui, quem Pius Papa Undécimus Sanctórum fastis adscrípsit.
<h>R</h>omæ, via Portuénsi, sanctórum Mártyrum Cyri et Ioánnis, qui, pro confessióne Christi, post multa torménta, cápite truncáti sunt.
<h>A</h>lexandríæ natális sancti Metráni Mártyris, qui, sub Décio Imperatóre, cum ad iussiónem Paganórum nollet ímpia verba proférre, hi totum eius corpus fústibus collisérunt, vultúmque et óculos præacútis cálamis terebrántes, cum cruciátibus expulérunt ipsum extra urbem, ibíque lapídibus oppréssum interemérunt.
<h>I</h>bídem sanctórum Mártyrum Saturníni, Thyrsi et Victóris.
<h>I</h>tem Alexandríæ sanctórum Mártyrum Tharsícii, Zótici, Cyríaci et Sociórum.
<h>C</h>ýzici, in Hellespónto, sanctæ Tryphǽnæ Mártyris, quæ, plúrimis torméntis superátis, a tauro demum necáta, martýrii palmam proméruit.
<h>M</h>útinæ sancti Geminiáni Epíscopi, miraculórum glória conspícui.
<h>I</h>n Província Mediolanénsi sancti Iúlii, Presbýteri et Confessóris, témpore Imperatóris Theodósii.
<h>N</h>eápoli sancti Francísci Xavérii-Maríæ Biánchi, Confessóris, Clérici Reguláris sancti Pauli, signis, donis cæléstibus et admirábili patiéntia illústris, quem Pius Papa Duodécimus ad suprémos honóres Sanctórum éxtulit.
<h>R</h>omæ sanctæ Marcéllæ Víduæ, cuius præcláras laudes beátus Hierónymus scripsit.
<h>I</h>tem Romæ Beátæ Ludovícæ Albertóniæ, Víduæ Románæ, ex tértio Ordine sancti Francísci, virtútibus claræ.
<h>E</h>ódem die Translátio sancti Marci Evangelístæ, cum sacrum eius corpus ex Alexandría, a bárbaris tunc occupáta, Venétias allátum, ibídem in maióri Ecclésia, eius nómine consecráta, honorificentíssime cónditum fuit.
<r>℣.</r> Et álibi aliórum plurimórum sanctórum Mártyrum et Confessórum, atque sanctárum Vírginum.
<r>℟.</r> Deo grátias.
b.df59b821e7:
<h>Martyrology</h>
<c>J</c>anuary 31st 2027, the 23rd day of the Moon,
<h>A</h>t Turin, St. John Bosco, confessor and founder of the Salesians and the founder of the Institute of the Daughters of Mary Auxiliatrix, known for his zeal for souls and propagation of the Faith, whom Pope Pius XI enrolled amongst the saints.
<h>U</h>pon the same 31st day of January, were born into a better life:
<h>A</h>t Rome, upon the way to Porto, the holy martyrs Cyrus and John, who suffered many torments for confessing Christ, and were beheaded, (in the fourth century.)
<h>A</h>t Alexandria, the holy martyr Metranus. In the time of the Emperor Decius he refused to utter unlawful words at the command of the Pagans. Wherefore they bruised his whole body with cudgels, pierced his face and eyes with sharp reeds, and continued to torture him while they cast him out of the city, where they stoned him to death, (in the year 249.)
<h>T</h>here, likewise, the holy martyrs Saturninus, Thyrsus, and Victor.
<h>I</h>n the same city, the holy martyrs Tharsicius, Zoticus, Cyriacus, and their Companions.
<h>A</h>t Cyzicus, on the Hellespont, the holy martyr Triphenes, who overcame diverse torments, and then gained the palm of martyrdom by being killed by a bull.
<h>A</h>t Modena, holy Geminian, (after the year 390,) Bishop of that see, famous for miracles.
<h>I</h>n the province of Milan, in the time of the Emperor Theodosius, (fifth century,) the holy Confessor Julius the Priest.
<h>A</h>t Rome, (in the year 410,) the holy widow Marcella, whose excellences have been written by blessed Jerome.
<h>A</h>t Rome, likewise, the blessed widow Louisa Albertoni, (in the year 1530,) of the 3rd Order of St. Francis, illustrious for her graces.
<h>U</h>pon the same day is commemorated the translation of the holy Evangelist Mark, when (in the year 831) his sacred body was taken from Alexandria, in Egypt, already occupied by the Mohammedans, and brought to Venice, where it is honourably buried in the great cathedral church consecrated in his name.
<r>℣.</r> And elsewhere many other holy martyrs, confessors, and holy virgins.
<r>℟.</r> Thanks be to God.
b.1df2a81061:
<h>Capitulum Hymnus Versus</h>
<r>2 Cor 1:3-4</r>
<c>B</c>enedíctus Deus, et Pater Dómini nostri Iesu Christi, Pater misericordiárum, et Deus totíus consolatiónis, qui consolátur nos in omni tribulatióne nostra.
<r>℟.</r> Deo grátias.

<r>℟.</r> Benedícens ergo illi, Noë ait: Nequáquam ultra maledícam terræ propter hóminem:
* Ad imáginem quippe Dei factus est homo.
<r>℣.</r> Hoc erit signum fœ́deris inter me et inter terram: arcum meum ponam in núbibus cæli.
<r>℟.</r> Ad imáginem quippe Dei factus est homo.
<r>℣.</r> Glória Patri, et Fílio, * et Spirítui Sancto.
<r>℟.</r> Ad imáginem quippe Dei factus est homo.

<r>Hymnus</r>
<c>O</c> lux beáta Trínitas,
Et principális Únitas,
Iam sol recédit ígneus,
Infúnde lumen córdibus.

<h>T</h>e mane laudum cármine,
Te deprecémur véspere:
Te nostra supplex glória
Per cuncta laudet sǽcula.

<h>D</h>eo Patri sit glória,
Eiúsque soli Fílio,
Cum Spíritu Paráclito,
Et nunc, et in perpétuum.
Amen.

<r>℣.</r> Vespertína orátio ascéndat ad te, Dómine.
<r>℟.</r> Et descéndat super nos misericórdia tua.
b.eab68ef4aa:
<h>Chapter Hymn Verse</h>
<r>2 Cor 1:3-4</r>
<c>B</c>lessed be the God and Father of our Lord Jesus Christ, the Father of mercies, and the God of all comfort, who comforteth us in all our tribulation.
<r>℟.</r> Thanks be to God.

<r>℟.</r> Benedícens ergo illi, Noë ait: Nequáquam ultra maledícam terræ propter hóminem:
* Ad imáginem quippe Dei factus est homo.
<r>℣.</r> Hoc erit signum fœ́deris inter me et inter terram: arcum meum ponam in núbibus cæli.
<r>℟.</r> Ad imáginem quippe Dei factus est homo.
<r>℣.</r> Glory be to the Father, and to the Son, * and to the Holy Ghost.
<r>℟.</r> Ad imáginem quippe Dei factus est homo.

<r>Hymn</r>
<c>O</c> Trinity of blessed Light,
O Unity of sovereign might,
as now the fiery sun departs,
shed Thou Thy beams within our hearts.

<h>T</h>o Thee our morning song of praise,
to Thee our evening prayer we raise;
Thee may our glory evermore
in lowly reverence adore.

<h>A</h>ll laud to God the Father be;
all praise, Eternal Son, to Thee;
all glory, as is ever meet,
to God the Holy Paraclete.
Amen.

<r>℣.</r> Let the evening prayer ascend unto thee, O Lord.
<r>℟.</r> And let there descend upon us thy mercy.

b.19bf68cf2a:
<h>Oratio</h>
<r>℣.</r> Dómine, exáudi oratiónem meam.
<r>℟.</r> Et clamor meus ad te véniat.
<c>O</c>rémus.
<c>D</c>eus, qui cónspicis, quia ex nulla nostra actióne confídimus: concéde propítius; ut, contra advérsa ómnia Doctóris géntium protectióne muniámur.
<h>P</h>er Dóminum nostrum Iesum Christum, Fílium tuum: qui tecum vivit et regnat in unitáte Spíritus Sancti, Deus, per ómnia sǽcula sæculórum.
<r>℟.</r> Amen.
b.3d12ca300c:
<h>Prayer</h>
<r>℣.</r> O Lord, hear my prayer.
<r>℟.</r> And let my cry come unto thee.
<c>L</c>et us pray.
<c>O</c> God, Who seest that we put not our trust in anything that we do, mercifully grant that through the protection of the Teacher of the Gentiles we may be defended against all adversity.
<h>T</h>hrough Jesus Christ, thy Son our Lord, Who liveth and reigneth with thee, in the unity of the Holy Ghost, God, world without end.
<r>℟.</r> Amen.
